text:
I propose six WebMCP tools covering the complete reversible MED+250 visitor journey while keeping pharmacy dispatch behind the existing human-controlled WhatsApp and location checks.

- `ask_site` returns site-authored guidance and policies.
- `search_products` searches and visibly filters the public catalogue.
- `get_product_details` returns details and opens the product page.
- `add_to_order_basket` adds an approved item and opens the basket.
- `update_order_basket` changes or removes basket items.
- `prepare_order_request` opens request details but stops before location, OTP and submission.

Two defaults need attention: include the great-to-have basket-update tool, and build `ask_site` from MED+250's own static content because there is no existing search endpoint. Review descriptions and parameters, comment on any tool, then submit the plan to approve implementation.

Runtime review found one wiring adjustment. Connected/live MED+250 can keep using the same-origin Worker catalogue API. Local preview intentionally has no Worker API, so `search_products` needs to fall back to the marketplace's existing in-memory catalogue search and still apply the same visible filters. This adds no endpoint and sends no data externally. Approve this narrow fallback to continue verification, or comment with a different preview behavior.

Verification is complete for all six approved tools. The local preview fallback returned and visibly rendered matching products; the full local Worker journey verified site guidance, catalogue search, product-detail navigation, basket add/update/removal, and request preparation. Basket-only tools registered only while the basket was non-empty, and `/privacy` exposed only `ask_site`. The flow stopped before location sharing, WhatsApp OTP, prescription selection, submission, or pharmacy contact. Browser diagnostics were clean; focused tests, lint, and the production-style build passed.
